hints: Look closely from the lumen outwards in the photo. Notice the hair-like edge on the inner cells and the pale, rounded cells mixed in, then the thin dark band and the pale bubbly tissue at the bottom right.

Recall how trachea, bronchus and alveolus differ. Which one has ciliated epithelium plus goblet cells, a middle layer of elastic fibres and smooth muscle, and an outer supporting layer of cartilage that is not a complete ring?
walkthrough:
**Read the image from inside to outside**

Start at the white lumen on the left. You can see a tall epithelium with tiny cilia on top and paler goblet cells in between. Just below it is a thin, dark, wavy band of elastic fibres and muscle. Further out you see darker glandular tissue and then a large pale area with scattered cells in lacunae.

That pale area is cartilage.

**Match each layer to airway histology**

Ciliated epithelium plus mucus-secreting goblet cells is the classic cleaning lining of the larger airways. Elastic fibres allow stretch and recoil during breathing. Cartilage gives support to keep the airway open.

A very thin squamous lining with many capillaries would be an alveolus, not this thick ciliated lining.

**Choose between bronchus and trachea**

Both trachea and bronchus have this basic plan, but the trachea is supported by a continuous C-shaped ring of cartilage, while a bronchus is supported by irregular plates or islands of cartilage.

Here the cartilage at the bottom right is a discrete plate, not a continuous ring, with glands nearby. That fits a bronchus best, which is option C.

options.A: Close but incomplete and in the wrong order. It misses the goblet cells and puts cartilage before elastic fibres, while the photo shows epithelium, then elastic fibres, then cartilage outside.
options.B: This describes an alveolus with very thin squamous epithelium, elastic walls and surrounding capillaries for gas exchange. The image shows tall ciliated cells and thick cartilage, so it cannot be B.
options.C: Perfect match. Inner ciliated epithelium with goblet cells, middle elastic fibres, and outer supporting cartilage plate describes this bronchus section.
options.D: The inner lining part is right, but a continuous ring of cartilage is the trachea. This image shows only a plate or island of cartilage, typical of a bronchus, not a continuous ring.
